title: Cretaceous zhelestid mammals are zalambdalestoids.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: paywalled, no PMCID, no full text, no supplement listing, no accessions, no NCBI links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI. One web search found only press coverage and the Nature landing page; no MorphoBank project number or matrix file was located.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract and press coverage only: the paper describes one new fossil specimen (Tamirkhan balcarceli) and places it in a phylogeny built from an expanded version of a MorphoBank anatomical character matrix (a table of coded skull, tooth and skeleton traits per species). Taxon and character counts were not seen.

a1_downloadable.note: No data file found: paywalled paper, no supplement listing, no repository hit; the MorphoBank project is mentioned in press coverage but no project ID was found. Not verified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The paper's output is a phylogenetic placement (a tree), not a measured label column; any ML target (e.g. clade membership) would have to be constructed from the inferred tree.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be coded morphological characters per taxon; not seen.

a4_units_stated.note: Characters are discrete coded states, not units; not checked.

a5_enough_rows.note: Rows would be taxa (species) in a fossil-mammal character matrix, which number in the tens to low hundreds, far below the ~400 minimum; exact count not seen.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: a character matrix would be well under 10 MB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem; estimated, not checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any clade label would come from the authors' own phylogenetic analysis of the same characters, so it is computed from the features (circular).

honest_claim_h3: None possible: this is a single-specimen fossil description with a phylogeny of at most a few hundred taxa, not a labelled dataset.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use coded fossil tooth, skull and limb traits to predict which mammal group an extinct species belongs to.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per species in the anatomical trait table the authors used; number of species unknown (not seen), likely tens to low hundreds.
plain_idea.predict: Group membership of each species, which here comes from the authors' tree built from the same traits, so it is not an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It could flag fossils whose teeth mislead placement, but the tree-building software already does this properly and the sample is far too small for ML.

label_elsewhere.why: Not assessed; the project fails Part A.

ml_idea: Classify fossil taxa into clades from morphological character codes; rejected because the label is the phylogeny inferred from those same characters and there are too few taxa.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; project fails Part A before compute matters.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count taxa (rows) in the MorphoBank matrix; under 400 kills it, and the circular label kills it regardless.

verdict_reason: A paleontology paper describing one new fossil and a phylogeny from a paywalled, not-located morphological matrix. Fails A1 (no file found), A5 (taxa number at most in the hundreds) and A8 (any clade label is inferred from the same characters).
